issues.legal_issue: Summary eviction from land cannot be used to resolve a bona fide dispute over whether the land belongs to the government.
material_facts: The government sought to evict occupants summarily from land whose inclusion in an earlier acquisition was disputed.

A prior suit brought by the university for whose benefit acquisition was claimed had been dismissed: one plot was found not to have been acquired, and as to the other plots the university had failed to establish possession within the limitation period.
The government had not been a party to that suit, and the occupants and their predecessors had possessed the land for an appreciable period.

The occupants claimed through the original owner, and deciding the government’s title required resolving whether the land had been acquired and whether title had later been perfected by adverse possession.
issues.conclusion: The government could not evict the occupants summarily while the genuine dispute over title remained unresolved; the title questions had to be decided through an appropriate ordinary court proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2 and 3 of the Andhra Pradesh Land Encroachment Act, 1905, the summary eviction power in section 6 applies to unauthorised occupation of land that is government property and for which assessment is payable; section 7 requires notice before proceedings. Where government title is genuinely disputed and the occupant has a bona fide claim, the government cannot decide title unilaterally and then rely on section 6. Summary proceedings are not suited to adjudicating complicated title questions and are not due process for that purpose. The court cited no earlier case as the basis for this holding.

predicates.summary_eviction_proceeding: The government sought to remove an occupant through a summary statutory eviction process.
predicates.bona_fide_title_dispute: The government and occupant genuinely disputed whether the land belonged to the government, including whether it had been acquired or whether the occupant's predecessor had obtained title through long possession.
predicates.occupant_claims_title: The occupant asserted a claim to the land rather than occupying it without any claim of right.

issues.definition: When the government seeks summary eviction and the occupant asserts a claim amid a genuine dispute over government title, summary eviction is unavailable until the title dispute is adjudicated.

issues.legal_issue: The duration of an alleged encroachment alone does not determine whether summary eviction is available.
material_facts: The occupants and their predecessors had openly possessed the land for an appreciable period, with the alleged encroachment on some plots dating back to 1942.
The claim of government ownership depended on disputed acquisition and limitation issues, while the occupants claimed through the land’s original owner.

The High Court Division Bench had treated recent origin of an alleged encroachment as a condition for using the summary remedy; the Supreme Court held that this view could not be applied as an absolute rule.
issues.conclusion: The age of an alleged encroachment is not conclusive. The nature of the property and whether the occupant’s claim is bona fide are more important; appreciable open occupation may support a prima facie bona fide claim requiring impartial adjudication.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 6 and 7 of the Andhra Pradesh Land Encroachment Act, 1905, duration is relevant but does not itself decide whether summary eviction may be used. The court stated that the nature of the property and the bona fides of the occupant’s claim matter, and that appreciable open occupation may indicate a prima facie claim requiring adjudication through ordinary legal procedure. It noted the earlier view in Meherunnissa Begum v. State of A.P., affirmed by a Division Bench, but cautioned against stretching the recent-origin approach into an absolute rule.

predicates.summary_eviction_proceeding: The government sought to remove an occupant through a summary statutory eviction process.
predicates.alleged_encroachment_duration_is_conside: The age or length of the occupant's alleged encroachment was raised as a reason for deciding whether the summary process could be used.

issues.definition: In a summary eviction proceeding, considering how long an alleged encroachment has lasted does not make duration alone decisive; the property and the occupant’s claim must also be assessed.
